gloss: haphazard; unplanned; playing it by ear

definitions.gloss: haphazard; unplanned; playing it by ear; random; improvised
definitions.explanation: Acting without a plan or preparation, just dealing with things as they come. Can describe either a carefree attitude or reckless disorganization.

examples.japanese: {行|い}き{当|あ}たりばったりの{旅|たび}が{好|す}きだ。
{計画|けいかく}を{立|た}てず、{行|い}き{当|あ}たりばったりで{行動|こうどう}した。
examples.english: I acted without making a plan, just playing it by ear.

examples.japanese: {行|い}き{当|あ}たりばったりの{経営|けいえい}では、いずれ{失敗|しっぱい}する。
examples.english: Haphazard management will eventually lead to failure.

notes:
Can carry either a positive or negative nuance depending on context. When describing travel or leisure, it suggests a carefree, adventurous spirit. In work or business contexts, it implies irresponsible lack of planning. Functions as a noun modified by の, or as an adverbial modifier with で.

ETYMOLOGY:
From {行|い}き{当|あ}たる (to come across by chance) + ばったり (suddenly encountering). The doubling creates an emphatic sense of doing whatever one happens upon.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {行|い}き{当|あ}たりばったりの{旅|たび}: an unplanned trip
- {行|い}き{当|あ}たりばったりの{生活|せいかつ}: an aimless lifestyle
- {行|い}き{当|あ}たりばったりで{決|き}める: to decide on the fly
- {行|い}き{当|あ}たりばったりに{行動|こうどう}する: to act haphazardly

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {出|で}たとこ{勝負|しょうぶ}: playing it by ear; taking one's chances — similar meaning but focuses more on the element of risk
- {無計画|むけいかく}: unplanned; without a plan — a more neutral, descriptive term
- {場当|ばあ}たり: ad hoc; improvised — often negative, implying stopgap measures without thinking ahead
